steps.analyst_reply: {"root_cause": "The single holistic question forces the model to guess the occupation from surface wording, and the errors split into three clean clusters: (1) surgeon bios that never say 'surgery' but signal it through orthopedics, sports medicine, spine/brain, or joint work (called physician); (2) physician bios that do say 'surgery' via OB/GYN or women's-health procedures like pelvic, gynecologic, or laser surgery (called surgeon); (3) 'Ms./Mr.' listings that 'specialize in' a surgical field such as neurological, orthopaedic, or plastic surgery but are labeled physician, a title regularity that holds in every labeled sample too. Targeted evidence questions on these three cues attack the majority of the 25 disagreements without touching the well-calibrated holistic feature.", "add_elements": [{"key": "orthopedic_sports_spine_focus", "question_type": "noul", "instructions": "Does the text say this person treats or specializes in orthopedics, sports medicine, bones, joints, the spine, or the brain (for example orthopedics, sports medicine, joint replacement, musculoskeletal injuries, or a brain-and-spine practice)?", "criteria": null}, {"key": "obgyn_womens_health_focus", "question_type": "noul", "instructions": "Does the text say this person practices obstetrics or gynecology or focuses on women's health (for example pap tests, infertility, or pelvic, gynecologic, or vaginal procedures)?", "criteria": null}, {"key": "non_doctor_title", "question_type": "noul", "instructions": "Does the text refer to this person with the title Ms., Mrs., or Mr. instead of Dr.?", "criteria": null}], "retire_elements": [], "reword_elements": []}
